Subject: HealthScope — model fit & safety follow-up (recommended models, prompt sets, next steps)

Hi Emily — great to meet today. Thanks for taking the time to walk through HealthScope's triage flow and safety constraints.

Recap / what we heard:
- Primary use: automated initial triage for clinician intake forms (text + short audio transcripts). Expected per-tenant throughput: ~400 reqs/min peak.
- Key quality needs: high refusal accuracy on disallowed PHI extraction, conservative handling of self-harm content, and stable intent classification for routing.
- Ops constraints: data residency in US, strict audit logging for decisions, and 99.9% inference availability SLA for live triage.

Recommended quick-start evaluation plan:
1) Model candidates to benchmark:
   - redwood-2.1-large (best throughput / safety baseline)
   - redwood-2.1-xl (higher quality, higher cost)
   - llama-2.2-13b-q4 (open variant for cost comparison)
2) Prompt sets attached: healthscope_prompt_set_v2.json (includes refusal / guardrail prompts and labeled examples)
3) Benchmarks & artifacts: model_benchmarks_v1.pdf + shared Drive link with perf traces and token-level costs.
4) Safety evals: small labeled corpus (safety_eval_samples.csv) focusing on PHI, suicidal ideation, and physician impersonation cases.

Immediate next steps I'd suggest:
- You share a small sample of anonymized transcripts (10-50) and any existing refusal rules by EOD Thu so we can run initial bench + refusal behavior analysis.
- We run a 72-hour eval across the three model candidates and return a one-page model recommendation with quality/cost tradeoffs.
- Technical follow-up call: Wed Jul 7 at 11am PT — Rafael will join to discuss guardrail implementation and audit logs. Can you confirm availability?

Attachments: healthscope_prompt_set_v2.json, model_benchmarks_v1.pdf, safety_eval_samples.csv

Thanks,

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: HealthScope — model fit & safety follow-up (recommended models, prompt sets, next steps)

Hi Emily — quick technical answers.

1) Refusal behavior:
- redwood-2.1-xl uses a combination of model fine-tuning and prompt-layer guardrails in our hosted product. By default the model has safety priors (trained refusal signals) but the strictness is tunable via the prompt and a policy mask layer. For your case we recommend a two-layer approach:
  a) Prompt-level guardrail that explicitly instructs the model to refuse disallowed extraction and to return a standard escalation token (e.g., "<ESCALATE>"). Example snippet we include in healthscope_prompt_set_v2.json:
     "If the user content contains unconsented Personal Health Information (PHI) or self-harm intent, respond with \"<ESCALATE>\" and a short refusal message. Do not attempt to paraphrase or complete PHI fields."
  b) Post-process policy check that inspects model outputs for PHI patterns (regex + ML-based matcher) and overrides with refusal if necessary.

2) Logs & retention:
- Redwood Private supports exportable per-request logs (prompt, full model response, token-level probabilities on request) and configurable retention. 12-month retention is supported for Private and Dedicated via our audit export (we'll include an export manifest in the eval report). Hosted customers can request longer retention with an add-on.

3) Eval metrics & tooling:
- We'll return: refusal precision/recall, false positive rate (legitimate content refused), classification accuracy for routing intents, latency p95, and cost per 1k tokens.
- Eval reproducibility: we run the eval with a pinned model snapshot and provide the evaluation harness (python scripts + dataset) in the Drive link. You can rerun locally against Private deployments.

I'll prepare a short tech note to attach to the eval deliverable that outlines the guardrail prompt templates and post-processing heuristics.

Best,
Rafael
